about.title: Laguna Beach Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Laguna Beach residents rely on a mix of local clinics and nearby Orange County hospitals for everything from routine care to surgical procedures, and most visits go exactly as expected. But when a provider's error causes real harm — a delayed cancer diagnosis, a surgical mistake, or a medication mix-up — the aftermath can be disorienting, especially while you're still trying to heal. California treats medical malpractice differently than an ordinary injury case: there are shorter timelines, a required pre-suit notice, and a medical expert almost always has to weigh in before a claim moves forward. LawProactive doesn't practice law or evaluate your medical records ourselves. What we do is connect people in Laguna Beach with an independent attorney in our network who handles these claims and can walk you through whether what happened meets California's legal standard for malpractice — a standard that requires more than just a disappointing result.

whyChoose.title: Why Laguna Beach Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand MICRA's Tight Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, so waiting to ask questions can cost you options.

items.title: We Know the 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed in California, the provider typically must receive 90 days' advance written notice — a step an independent attorney can help make sure isn't missed.

items.title: We Connect You to Attorneys Who Work With Medical Experts
items.desc: Because California almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim, we focus on connecting people with attorneys who already have those relationships in place.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result on its own doesn't prove malpractice occurred. There has to be evidence the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care, which is why a medical expert's review is typically required before a claim moves forward.

items.question: How much time do I have to bring a claim in Laguna Beach?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from when it happened, whichever comes first. There are some exceptions, so it's worth having an independent attorney look at your specific timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: Are there limits on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in medical malpractice claims, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic losses, such as medical bills and lost income, aren't subject to that same cap. An attorney can explain how this applies given your circumstances.

items.question: I live in Laguna Beach — does it matter which facility treated me?
items.answer: It can matter for practical reasons, like where records are held and which providers were involved, but the legal standards under California's MICRA rules apply regardless of which Orange County facility treated you. What matters most is documenting what happened and getting an independent review sooner rather than later.
